Stored cells of a covering

Source: R/covering.R
a5_covering_stored.Rd

Returns the cells a covering stores: its compacted cells, which have mixed resolutions, in curve order and without the compaction marker. Use them for index range queries. Each stored cell's descendants at the covering's resolution form one contiguous id range, given by a5_cell_children_range(), so a covering is the union of those ranges.

Usage

a5_covering_stored(x, simplify = TRUE)

Arguments

x

An a5_covering vector, or anything as_a5_covering() accepts.

simplify

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), return one flat a5_cell vector with the stored cells of every covering in turn. If FALSE, return an a5_cell_list with one element per covering; a missing covering gives an empty element.

Value

An a5_cell vector, or an a5_cell_list if simplify = FALSE.

Details

The stored cells are index parents, not geometric ones: their outlines do not nest, so do not draw them or use them as an area. Use a5_uncompact() for the cells a covering stands for.

See also

a5_uncompact() for the cells at the covering's resolution, a5_covering_resolution(), a5_cell_children_range().

Examples

cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 8)
disk <- a5_grid_disk(cell, k = 3)
stored <- a5_covering_stored(disk)
a5_get_resolution(stored)
#>  [1] 8 8 8 8 8 7 8 8 8 8 7 7 8 8 8 8 7 7

# one id range per stored cell, at the covering's resolution
a5_cell_children_range(stored, resolution = a5_covering_resolution(disk))
#>                  lo               hi
#> 1  6315880000000000 6315880000000000
#> 2  6315980000000000 6315980000000000
#> 3  6315d80000000000 6315d80000000000
#> 4  6315e80000000000 6315e80000000000
#> 5  6315f80000000000 6315f80000000000
#> 6  6316080000000000 6316380000000000
#> 7  6316580000000000 6316580000000000
#> 8  6316680000000000 6316680000000000
#> 9  6316780000000000 6316780000000000
#> 10 63bb280000000000 63bb280000000000
#> 11 63bb480000000000 63bb780000000000
#> 12 63bb880000000000 63bbb80000000000
#> 13 63bbc80000000000 63bbc80000000000
#> 14 63bbd80000000000 63bbd80000000000
#> 15 63bbe80000000000 63bbe80000000000
#> 16 63be380000000000 63be380000000000
#> 17 63be880000000000 63beb80000000000
#> 18 63bec80000000000 63bef80000000000
